translations.text: So he does not give the title of apostle here, because those to whom it was written are perfect, and there is no need to rebuke them.
He was a pupil of his.
That is, the ordering of the body of Christ.
That is, it shows that his prayer is unceasing and that it is for believers, "for the faithful".
That is, no one is dearer to me than another.
That is, because you used to fulfil and preach the gospel, as I do.
That is, it was preached to you.
That is, until this day.
That is, I am sure of this.
That is, he will carry it on with him to the end.
That is, of the separation of body and soul, or "of the judgement".
That is, as is fitting for me.
That is, a good opinion of them.
That is, I wish for good testimony of them.
That is, that is what I have had.
That is, fulfilling it and preaching it is what confirms the gospel.
That is, "to the glory of God", so that you might be my companions.
That is, it is God who knows, who knows my love for you.
That is, this is very dear to me.
That is, so that the love of God and of your neighbour may grow in you more and more, and better and better.
That is, in every perfect sense.
More excellent things.
That is, a sincerity eager to fulfil the gospel.
That is, through which there is eternal life.
That is, because [?] my preaching from my imprisonment, more will believe because of it.
royal house
i.e. it has become known even in the king's house, as it has become known in everyone's house.
i.e. they are bolder in preaching the gospel this time.
i.e. because I preach out of my bonds.
i.e. they are bold because of it, because they know that it is not for the sake of great glory that I endure this.
i.e. they are jealous that the preaching is mine rather than theirs.
i.e. those are good.
for good will
i.e. these are the same as 'qui bona voluntate' (those who preach out of good will).
i.e. it is for this that I endure tribulations.
i.e. against me, as though I would be jealous that my office should be taken in my place while I am in prison.
pretext
i.e. it is not done out of good will toward me.
i.e. so that I would have tribulation on top of tribulation, that is, being in prison and having my office taken.
in an ill [?] manner
i.e. about it, out of hatred of me, like the pseudo-apostles.
i.e. it is no trouble to me, so long as it is Christ whom they preach and everyone thinks on him.
i.e. 'significat humiliter' (he says it humbly): that I may endure the sufferings through your prayer.
i.e. through the presence of the Spirit.
i.e. according to the expectation that I await [?].
i.e. through fulfilling and preaching the gospel.
i.e. if I am alive, it will be to preach the name of Christ.
many would be sanctified through me
i.e. that too is profit.
i.e. whether it be death or life.
i.e., which of the two I should choose
i.e., this is what I myself desire first
i.e., that would be better in my view
i.e., this is one of the two straits that presses me
i.e., the need for your salvation through precept and teaching
i.e., that is what will happen there
i.e., only
i.e., that you may fulfil and preach the Gospel
i.e., whether I am far away or still near, may I hear nothing but good news of you
for
i.e., that is what he would like to hear, as it is written: 'They had one body and one soul.'
i.e., both in fulfilling and in preaching
i.e., do not give a foot of ground to the false apostles
i.e., it causes their death
i.e., enduring the persecutions is a cause of salvation for you
i.e., it is not only that you believe, but you also suffer tribulations for it
i.e., 'sit in Christo', i.e., let it be a consolation of love
let it be
i.e., let it be of mercy

Otherwise ... [?] three ... [?] on this text, i.e., it is related to the aforementioned rule, and in that way it is referred to Paul, i.e., what follows below is what has been heard and seen in his habits and his deeds. Otherwise, it refers to 'implete gaudium' etc.: this is my joy, 'si qua' etc. 'in Christo': let it be in Christ, if there is any joy for you, and in that way it does not refer to him. Otherwise, it is done directly [?], i.e., 'in Christo': let it be in Christ, etc.; or, if you have all these things, 'implete', i.e., do what you are told.
i.e., be as I have been in deeds and in habits
i.e., as I love you, let each of you love the others
i.e., let no one seek glory for himself
i.e., 'sint', i.e., let him seek it for his neighbour
i.e., let each consider the other nobler than himself
i.e. that he did not look at the gift that had been given to himself, but at the gift of the other.
i.e. it is not to himself that he has given the glory, but to the Father.
i.e. in the power and dignity of God.
i.e. recognition which is above every name, i.e. the glory of the Father.
i.e. every tongue.
It is not easy to hide it; more [people] know it [?].
i.e. that is dearer to me.

i.e. all good things, i.e. this is what he seeks from above, that it should not be difficult for you, for it is God [who works in you]. Gregory: So it is of man, through the devil, that he sins; but it is of God that he is able to avoid sin.
i.e. of God, not because of your merit.
i.e. so that there may be a reward for your labour.
i.e. without contention.
i.e. so that you may be like your Father.
i.e. of the Jews, i.e. for they are enemies and foes.
i.e. it wins glory for me on the Day of Judgement.
i.e. it is evident in you.
i.e. even if I go to martyrdom.
i.e. this is the offering, i.e. after your faith has been offered by me to God.
i.e. I will send.
i.e. my mind will be at ease once I hear your good news.
i.e. it is not for treasures or riches that Timothy has loved you.
i.e. everyone seeks his own glory, except Timothy.
i.e. in preaching.
i.e. nevertheless.
in the battle against the devil.
i.e. of what I needed.
i.e., he loved you.
i.e., he was in sickness, and that was a grief to you; but harder to him, however, was your sorrow than his own pain.
i.e., death was near to him.
i.e., his death.
i.e., your grief, or of my pain.
i.e., as you had joy before his sickness.
i.e., through your joy.
i.e., what was lacking of your perfection.
i.e., what I have preached.
i.e., let the joy be in Him.
i.e., it is not wearisome to me; it is profitable to you.
because it is for earthly glory that they do it.
the cutting of the flesh
i.e., 'cutting' he says [?], for it is not worth boasting of it; for even we, we do not boast of it, though we underwent it at the proper time, but in Christ Jesus.
the proper cutting
i.e., lest it should be said that the reason he was reproaching circumcision was that he had not been circumcised.
i.e., it is for that reason that he says this.
and not in circumcision
i.e., not in circumcision and freedom, though it would be easy for me.
i.e., if it is of freedom and circumcision that anyone boasts,
i.e., it is evident that I am a true Israelite: it is at the proper time that I was circumcised.
i.e., a side-pillar of sovereignty [or: half-share of sovereignty]
that is lineage.
i.e., legal righteousness, i.e., a legal commandment.
i.e., with regard to the law.
i.e. I have fought for it, going forward, until now.
i.e. I would part with them.
i.e. their worth to me is no greater than that.
i.e. so that Christ may be my wealth (my gain).
i.e. he shows here that it is the righteousness of Christ that sanctifies, and not the righteousness of the Law.
i.e. the form and shape of his death upon me.
in what way (if somehow)
i.e. for if we are in co-death (sharing his death), we shall be in co-exaltation (sharing his glory).
i.e. that I may be worthy of it, i.e. of the co-resurrection with Christ.
i.e. comprehendi ('to have attained'): that little is all the good I do.
i.e. I do not look behind me.
i.e. the things that I have not done until now.
i.e. what is before me.
victory [?] (the prize)

Fratres, ego, etc. Here he compares himself to a runner who runs toward the prize of victory, i.e. this is his custom: he does not count the part of the course that is behind him, only what is before him, until he has passed it and reaches the prize. Paul was like that, and so it is fitting for everyone to be, i.e. in constant penance, straight toward the prize, i.e. toward the heavenly reward.
i.e. except for this.
i.e. what I say.
i.e. be with us in it (literally: be of our share in it).
i.e. to that [rule] of the New Testament.
i.e. so that we may all bring it about equally.
i.e. do what I do.
i.e. be on your guard against that band.
i.e. they have the appearance of apostles, and they do not follow their ways.
i.e. I have indeed set it before you.
i.e. it is grievous to me.
i.e. when they say that it is the law that sanctifies, and not the cross of Christ.
i.e. for it is for the sake of food that they preach.
i.e. what they boast of will be shame and disgrace to them.
i.e. it is not so with us.
i.e. which he took from us, or our body.
i.e. so that it may be in glory after the resurrection, like the glory of his body.
i.e. the power of the Godhead that brings it about.
The proper name of a man, or of a woman, or 'true brother'.
i.e. in fulfilling it, not in preaching it.
i.e. a disciple of Peter; he too fulfilled it.
i.e. of the other helpers; he does not give their names here.
i.e. be gentle towards everyone.
i.e. to give you whatever you need.
i.e. let what you ask not be contrary to your salvation.
i.e. peace is nobler than every sense.
i.e. not every fair peace is the same, for every fair peace is fleeting and unstable until it reaches this one.
i.e. from here onward.
i.e. being without sin.
Generosity, i.e. towards God.
i.e. let their way of life [?] be godly.
i.e. let it be in good conduct.
i.e. it is not difficult for you.
i.e. all that I have done before you, do it yourselves.
i.e. if you are like that.
i.e. not to seek food from you.
i.e. (not) for shame, or (because) it is little that has been granted to me [?], as I know.
i.e. so that I am content with everything.
i.e. I have been taught to endure [?].
I have been taught abundance.
i.e. when you share it, you give offerings to us.
i.e. they did not give offerings to us, i.e. we did not accept their offerings, because their perfection did not seem enough to us; besides, they did not give anything that we asked for.
i.e. not everything was due to them by right; but you gave it because of your perfection.
only twice, i.e. secundo (a second time).
when I was there.
i.e. I do not ask for it now.
i.e. what has been brought from you.
i.e. because it was brought gladly.
i.e. he has all the more.
i.e. a sign of peace and of good fellowship.
i.e. greetings to you from them all.
greetings to you from everyone who is not there.
i.e. those of Caesar's household who have believed.
